clue.text: Sino-Tibetan turn of phrase

indicators.note: a turn of something gives it a twist, so the following word's letters are spun into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A linguist notes an idiom from a language of the Himalayas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn of phrase' reads as one idiom, but it splits into an anagram signal and its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sherpa people of Nepal speak a language of the Sino-Tibetan family, so the name serves as an example of that group.

clue.text: Assault over, start

parts.note: to strike is to hit or attack
time is up when it is over

explanation.surface: A battle report: the attack is finished, and something else begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pits 'over' against 'start' as opposites, but together they combine into one phrasal verb meaning begin.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike up a conversation or a tune is to begin it, so the phrasal verb is a synonym for start.

clue.text: Dainty, a little thin, I flew upward

indicators.note: in a down clue, travelling upward means reading from the bottom back to the top
only a little of the following words is taken, a short run of their letters

parts.note: the run of letters sits inside these words, read backwards

explanation.surface: A slender creature describes floating lightly skyward.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'flew' back through 'I' and into 'thin'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin means small and delicately formed, like an elf, which is close to dainty.

clue.text: Down in perfect time

parts.note: a plum job or role is an ideal, excellent one
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Something descends with flawless timing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like a direction; it is the soft feathers of a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is fluffy feathering, and plumage is a bird's covering of feathers, so one is a kind of the other.

clue.text: Idiot nicking empty space in cupboard

indicators.note: nicking means stealing, so the first part grabs and holds the other inside it

parts.note: a clot is British slang for a fool

indicators.note: emptied of its contents, a word keeps only its first and last letters

parts.note: only the outside letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: A fool steals floor space inside a storage cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A closet is a small room or tall cupboard for storage, a synonym of cupboard.

clue.text: Way to eat dip, Italian food

indicators.note: something that eats takes the other thing inside itself

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road or way
to sag is to droop or dip

explanation.surface: Advice on eating a dip, alongside a dish from Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Way to eat' suggests a method of dining; it is a road swallowing a word for droop.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is a baked Italian dish of flat pasta sheets layered with sauce.

clue.text: Exercise in demolishing of dessert, one going fast

indicators.note: one item is placed in the middle of the other
a demolished thing is broken up, so the letters of the next word are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Working out by polishing off a pudding, a quick eater bolts it down.
explanation.definitionFit: A speedster is a person or vehicle that travels at high speed.

clue.text: Fish has to dry up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: taken as written
brut describes very dry champagne

explanation.surface: A fish taken out of water must dry out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry up' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'dry' is the wine term and 'up' turns the letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: The turbot is a large European flatfish prized as food.

clue.text: Intellectual supporting launch

parts.note: to be pro something is to be in favour of it
to found a company is to launch it

explanation.surface: A thinker backs the start of a new venture.
explanation.definitionFit: Profound means showing deep insight or knowledge, close in sense to intellectual.

clue.text: Show leader of race in great condition

parts.note: a demon at something is a great performer at it

indicators.note: the single letter goes inside the rest

parts.note: a state is a condition

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter only

explanation.surface: A display shows the front runner in fine form.
explanation.definitionFit: To demonstrate something is to show it clearly or prove it.

clue.text: Range sent back, somewhat bizarre I see

indicators.note: something sent back travels the other way, so the letters are read right to left
only some of the following words is used, a short run of their letters

parts.note: the run starts in 'see' and runs back into 'bizarre'

explanation.surface: Someone notes how strangely a mountain range was returned.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a long jagged mountain chain, a kind of range.

clue.text: A piece, not entirely similar

indicators.note: something not entirely present has lost a part, here its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
the king is a chess piece

explanation.surface: Two fragments that almost match one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piece' suggests a portion; here it is a chessman, cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Akin means related or of a similar nature, a synonym of similar.

clue.text: Give old teacher a gun for ultimate war

parts.note: to give someone a weapon is to arm them
aged means old
a don is a university teacher
completes the verb phrase begun by 'Give'; it adds no letters of its own

explanation.surface: Handing a weapon to an elderly schoolmaster as the final battle looms.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a sentence: arm the aged don. The verb and its object come out in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Armageddon is the prophesied last battle between good and evil, hence a final, catastrophic conflict.

clue.text: Rogue channel out to catch me — spam!

indicators.note: to catch something is to take it into one's hold, so one part encloses the other
a rogue element behaves wildly, so the letters go astray from their order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that a wayward TV channel keeps flooding someone with junk email.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spam' looks like junk mail; it is the brand of tinned pork.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is a brand of tinned pork, the best-known example of this processed cold meat.

clue.text: Bully threw one over barrier

indicators.note: in a down clue, one part sits over the next, so they follow in order from the top

parts.note: to cast is to throw
the Roman numeral for one
a gate is a barrier

explanation.surface: A thug lobbed someone over a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bully' looks like a noun for the thug; it is the verb, to harass or berate.
explanation.definitionFit: To castigate is to rebuke severely, overlapping with bully in the sense of harshly berating someone.

clue.text: Little bit cross, writer in stitches, oddly

indicators.note: the cross and the writer are placed inside the other letters
taking a word oddly keeps its first, third, fifth and seventh letters

parts.note: the odd-numbered letters only
a cross is the letter X
a pen is a writing tool

explanation.surface: A slightly cross author is laughing helplessly, oddly enough.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bit' was British slang for a small coin, as in a threepenny bit; the sixpence was a small pre-decimal coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixpence, or sixpenny bit, was a small old British coin, so it is a little coin called a bit.

clue.text: Nitwit, a centrist struggling to impress supporter

indicators.note: to impress is to press in, so the one item is pushed inside the other
something struggling writhes about, so the letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A foolish moderate politician tries hard to win over a backer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scatterbrain is a disorganised, forgetful person, close to a nitwit or fool.

clue.text: An Italian poet moving quite slowly

parts.note: taken as written
Dante Alighieri wrote the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: A description of an Italian poet walking at a leisurely pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is the musical tempo marking for a moderately slow, walking pace.

clue.text: Caution in store

definitions.meaning: first meaning: restraint or reticence in manner
second meaning: a supply kept back for later use

explanation.walkthrough: 'In store' reads as a phrase, but 'in' just joins two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both cautious restraint in behaviour and a stock held back for future need.

clue.text: Eye record in match

indicators.note: the first item is placed inside the second

parts.note: a peer is an equal, someone who matches you
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: An eye-witness record from a sports match.
explanation.definitionFit: Peepers is informal slang for eyes, so one eye is a peeper.

clue.text: Where, for example, cocktails are served in jail

definitions.text: Where, for example, cocktails are served
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the staff mixing drinks stand on the far side of the counters in pubs
second meaning: locked up in a cell

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is cryptic: drinks are prepared on the staff's side of the counter.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for imprisoned, and literally describes the position of staff serving drinks.

clue.text: 25 Across, short implement knocked over

indicators.note: a thing knocked over ends up the other way round
something cut short has lost its end

parts.note: a spoon is an eating implement

explanation.surface: An exclamation as a tool is clumsily toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 Across is DEAR ME, an exclamation of mild dismay.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are interjections of mild dismay at a small mistake, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Different native shunning principal

indicators.note: the principal letter is the first one, and shunning it means it is left out

parts.note: one's native tongue or country is one's mother tongue or country

explanation.surface: A local stands apart by avoiding the head teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Principal' suggests a head teacher; it means the leading letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Other means distinct or not the same, a synonym of different.

clue.text: Twist right in home of flamenco?

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the country

parts.note: flamenco dance comes from southern Spain
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Turning an ankle in a dance hall where flamenco is performed.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprain a joint is to twist it so the ligaments are wrenched.

clue.text: US lawman requiring perfect listening device

parts.note: Wyatt Earp was a famous marshal of the Wild West
to hone a skill is to perfect it

explanation.surface: An American marshal needs a flawless bugging device.
explanation.definitionFit: An earphone is a small speaker worn at the ear for hearing audio.

clue.text: Wine bottles I say smelt bad

indicators.note: something that bottles another holds it inside

parts.note: red wine
both are exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: A drinker exclaims that the bottled wine had a foul odour.
explanation.definitionFit: To reek is to give off a strong, unpleasant smell, so the past tense fits smelt bad.

clue.text: Model remade well!

indicators.note: to model clay is to shape it into a new form, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A fashion model has been given a makeover, and it was well done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a noun; it is the verb that reshapes the letters, and 'well!' is an exclamation, not an adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Well! used as an exclamation of surprise is a synonym for this mild interjection.
